topics.topic: A08 vs A09 boundary for manifest instance validity checks (record-time vs send-time)
questions: Which exact checks are performed under A08 rule 6 versus deferred to A09 rule 6 at send time?
If `api_base_url` is present but syntactically invalid/unparseable, must proposal/accept fail as manifest mismatch, or is this only a send-time `operation_failed` pre-send failure?
If the selected instance now has duplicate required-header names (case-insensitive), which check rejects it at send time and what exact failure detail is recorded?

quotes: When the record cannot be read or fails one of rule 5's checks of the record itself — not those of the instance, which are A09 rule 6's own — the entry is absent, the operation is no longer invocable, or its digest differs from the binding's pin, nothing is sent and the element concludes `operation_failed` with detail `binding_stale` (A09 rule 6).
the installation selects no instance for the service or that instance has no `api_base_url` or names one required header twice, names compared without regard to case;

The checks run in this order and the first that fails is named: the binding is stale or no longer invocable (A08 rule 6); the instance or its address is missing or not allowed (rules 1 and 4), or its credential cannot be resolved (A17); an input value cannot be placed in the request (rule 2).
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats selected-instance defects (for example duplicate required-header names or invalid/missing address form) as A08 stale-record failures (`binding_stale`, and possibly proposal/accept refusal as manifest mismatch); another defers them to A09 pre-send instance checks (`operation_failed` with an instance/address check detail) after proposal/accept succeeds. Agents and the owner notice different proposal/accept outcomes and different run failure reasons.
judgement.why: The rules split record checks from instance checks but do not close exactly which instance-validity conditions belong to each side in all cases.

topics.topic: Approval lifecycle rules: recovery-time state changes, which approval is consumed, and resend eligibility cutoffs
questions: On restart recovery of `in_flight` attempts, must linked approvals always be moved to `used`, and at what exact step?
If more than one approved, unused approval for the same run/node/element matches the same request_digest, which approval record must be consumed and marked `used`?

What is the exact cutoff when there are multiple `not_applied` resolutions for the same element (or an approval requested before resolution but decided after)? Which approvals are valid for the resend?

quotes: Before sending a `state-transition`, `external-effect` or `destructive` node, the kernel needs one of: an approved, unused EffectApproval M24 of that run, node and element whose `request_digest` equals the digest of the request about to be sent (rule 7) —
When both exist, the approval is used and recorded as the authority.
A fresh approval after `not_applied` is one requested after that resolution; approvals recorded before it never count.
A crash between those two calls is the `in_flight` case of rule 4, whose recovery also marks that approval `used`.
judgement.divergence: One implementation deterministically consumes a specific matching approval (for example earliest matching) and, after each `not_applied`, allows only approvals requested after the latest such resolution; another consumes a different matching approval (or any matching one) and/or accepts an older approval. The owner and agents notice different approval statuses/authority IDs and different whether a resend asks again or sends immediately.
judgement.why: The texts define eligibility and freshness but do not define tie-breaking among multiple simultaneously eligible approvals nor the exact repeated-resolution cutoff rule for all multi-attempt histories.

topics.topic: Activation failure classification for unknown flow/version references
questions: If activation is requested for a non-existent flow_id or flow_version_id, is the refusal `unknown reference`, `unproven`, or another failure?

topics.topic: Deterministic attribution order when both source and target validation could fail
questions: If both source-side and target-side validations could fail for the same transferred value, which node is deterministically blamed and recorded first?

topics.topic: Exact placeholder grammar/parsing rules for manifest-declared paths
questions: What exact parser defines placeholders in declared paths (e.g., nested braces, unmatched braces, literal braces)?

topics.topic: Externally visible behavior when runtime symlink/store-call failures occur during mutating operations
questions: When this happens during run advancement (or any mutating request), what externally visible outcome is required: request refusal only, kernel stop, run marked failed, or retry behavior?
For a `many` value port, which byte size is enforced for `stored_value_bytes_max`?
Where is `applied_outputs_unknown` represented for later checks/readers, and exactly how do dependants detect this as failed if NodeExecution status remains `outcome_unknown`?

topics.topic: What event unblocks dependants after `service_unreachable` (owner resolution vs later successful resume/send)
questions: For dependants blocked by `service_unreachable`, what event unblocks them: only owner resolution (as written), or a later successful resend via `resume`?

topics.topic: `failure_detail` encoding requirements when captured error bytes are non-UTF-8
questions: How must `failure_detail` be produced when the captured error body bytes are not valid UTF-8?
